chunks.text:
|Key Message

Grades of recommendation, A-E are based on evidence graded using SIGN criteria (appendix VI)

• Egg allergy is an adverse immunological reaction induced by egg protein.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0022
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
This guideline focuses on type-1 IgE-mediated allergy to egg.
• The prevalence of egg allergy is estimated at approximately 2% in children and 0.1% in adults in the United Kingdom (Grade of recommendation = B).
• Allergic sensitization to egg, without a history of reacting, is common in infancy and should not prevent the introduction of egg into the diet, because this carries a risk of unnecessary dietary exclusion (Grade of recommendation =D).
• Egg allergy presents most commonly in infancy, usually after the first apparent ingestion, with rapid onset of erythema, urticaria, angio-oedema and/or vomiting (Grade of recommendation = B).
• Severe reactions involving respiratory or cardiovascular symptoms, presenting with cough, wheeze, breathing difficulty or pallor and floppiness are uncommon (Grade of recommendation = B).
• The clinical diagnosis is made by the rapid onset of typical symptoms (usually within minutes) after ingestion of egg (Grade of recommendation = B).
• Reaction severity is related to the amount of egg ingested and the degree of cooking, with raw egg white being the most allergenic (Grade of recommendation =D).
• The presence of egg-specific immunoglobulin E (IgE) or positive egg skin prick test (SPT) is useful in the management of moderatesevere cases or where there is diagnostic uncertainty (Grade of recommendation = B).
• The reported level of egg-specific IgE required to support a diagnosis varies between studies.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0023
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
It is not possible to identify a single cut-off value for egg-specific IgE which is ‘diagnostic’ for egg allergy at all ages (Grade of recommendation = B).
• An egg SPT weal of 3 mm or more in combination with a clinical history is considered adequate to confirm a diagnosis of egg allergy in most cases (Grade of recommendation = B).
• Clinical severity cannot be judged on basis of SPT weal size or serum-specific IgE alone (Grade of recommendation = C).
• In the absence of having a suspected reaction to egg, patients should not routinely be tested for egg allergy (Grade of recommendation = D).
• A food challenge may be necessary to confirm or refute conflicting history and test results but is rarely required in practice to confirm the diagnosis of egg allergy (Grade of recommendation = D).
• Following an acute allergic reaction to egg, egg avoidance advice is the cornerstone of management (Grade of recommendation = D).
• Most infants with egg allergy should continue to breastfeed, with their mother on an unrestricted diet (Grade of recommendation

= D).

• Mothers breastfeeding egg-allergic infants may wish to try egg exclusion if their infants have persistent eczema and egg is a trigger, or if the infant is suspected of reacting to maternal egg ingestion (Grade of recommendation = C).
• Referral to a dietician is required if there are multiple food allergies, nutritional concerns or help needed following the reintroduction ladder (Grade of recommendation = D).
• Referral to a dietician is needed for children with severe egg allergy for advice about strict egg avoidance (Grade of recommendation = D).
• Mild egg allergy usually resolves.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0024
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Attempts to introduce baked egg as an ingredient (e.g.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0025
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
in cake) may be made from the age of 12 months, or 6 months from the last reaction (Grade of recommendation = B).
• Regular ingestion of baked egg may promote tolerance (Grade of recommendation = C).
• Once loosely cooked egg is tolerated, egg allergy is outgrown and egg should be eaten as part of the normal diet (Grade of recommendation = D).
• Resolution occurs gradually over time.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0026
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
Assessment for reintroduction of baked egg in all infants/young children presenting with egg allergy is advised as prolonged total exclusion may lead to more persistent allergy and increases dietary and social exclusion (Grade of recommendation = B).
• Children with mild-moderate symptoms can reintroduce egg at home, starting with baked egg in small amounts (Grade of recommendation = D).
• Children with a history of a severe egg reaction or severe eczema and faltering growth are more likely to have persistent disease and avoidance and reintroduction should be guided by a specialist allergy service (Grade of recommendation = D).

• Egg allergy in infancy is associated with an increased risk of developing peanut allergy.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0027
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
This may be prevented by the early introduction of peanut into the diet (Grade of recommendation = B).
• New onset egg allergy in adults is rare; it is usually more severe and persists (Grade of recommendation = D).
• All children with egg allergy should receive the MMR immunization in primary care (Grade of recommendation = B).
• Children with egg allergy can receive the nasal live attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) and most children and adults can receive the intramuscular influenza vaccine in primary care, unless they have had anaphylaxis to egg requiring admission to intensive care (Grade of recommendation = B).
• Yellow Fever vaccines contain detectable, but not quantified amounts of egg protein.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0028
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
If these vaccines are required, the eggallergic patient should be referred to an allergy specialist with access to a designated yellow fever vaccination centre for assessment and immunization (Grade of recommendation = B).
| |---| |BOX 1 Which patients with egg allergy should be referred to an allergy clinic

• History of moderate to severe reaction (See Box 4)
• Where there is diagnostic uncertainty
• Egg allergy in association with other IgE mediated food allergies
• Severe eczema in children on an egg-containing diet
• Allergy to baked egg which persists beyond the common age of resolution (6-7 years).
• Adult-onset egg allergy
• Egg allergy with requirement for yellow fever immunisation
• Any child wishing to reintroduce egg but unable due to high anxiety.
• Egg allergic patients on biologics and immunosuppressants
| |---| development.

chunks.text:
#### 2 | DEFINITION AND MECHANISM

Egg allergy is an adverse immunological reaction, most often induced by the proteins in egg white, usually ovalbumin (Gal d 2) and/ or ovomucoid (Gal d 1) mediated by egg-specific IgE.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0036
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Ovomucoid is heat stable and immunodominant.2,3 Late-phase and delayed hypersensitivity reactions also occur, typically in eczema.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0037
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: The production of egg-specific IgE is a pre-requisite for developing type-1 hypersensitivity to egg.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0038
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
The route, timing and dose of

egg protein exposure, resulting in sensitization and clinical allergy, are unknown.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0039
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
#### 3 | PREVALENCE

The EuroPrevall birth cohort reports that challenge confirmed hen's egg allergy, in children at 2 years of age, is about 1% across Europe and 2% in the UK.4,5 Egg allergy is much less common in adults.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0040
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: The prevalence of egg allergy in the adult population has been estimated at 0.1%.6 Newly diagnosed egg allergy in adults is rare.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0041
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
#### 4 | RISK FACTORS

Egg allergy in children is associated with eczema and rhinitis.7 Eczema is a significant risk factor for egg allergy.8 The onset of eczema predates egg allergy by an average of 3.5 months and the likelihood of egg allergy increases with the severity of eczema.7 Boys with early-life eczema have the highest prevalence of egg sensitization.9 Egg allergy is not associated with age of introduction of egg into the diet.7 Children who received antibiotics in the first week of life are more likely to develop egg allergy.7 Egg allergy may occur in association with other food allergies, such as cow's milk protein or peanut.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0042
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:

• Most children should receive a clinical diagnosis without resorting to food challenge.
• If the history is unclear, a negative skin prick test can exclude egg allergy.
• Skin prick test weal size or level of specific IgE does not predict the severity of allergic reactions to egg29.
• The severity of a reaction depends on the amount of allergen ingested, the matrix, how well it is cooked and concomitant asthma, exercise or illness.
| |---| #### 5 | CLINICAL PRESENTATION AND SEVERITY The onset of egg allergy is usually observed early in life, in children with eczema and atopy.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0043
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
Egg allergy most commonly presents after the first apparent ingestion.8,10,11 Most reactions occur to lightly cooked egg, with reactions to baked egg and raw egg being less common.10 Clinical reactions include urticaria and/or angio-oedema in 80–90% (within minutes) and gastrointestinal symptoms in 10–44% (within 2 h).10,12–14

Most reactions occurring in the community are mild, with facial erythema and/or urticaria.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0044
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: In children, a mild reaction is characterized by cutaneous symptoms on significant exposure (e.g.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0045
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: a mouthful of cooked egg) sometimes associated with a single vomit.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0046
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: A hoarse cry, change in voice pitch, cough, stridor or wheeze indicates involvement of the respiratory tract and a more severe reaction.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0047
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Occasionally young children develop pallor and floppiness.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0048
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
Moderate to severe reactions with respiratory symptoms are less common; 5–10% in challenge studies, but less in the community, where the initial triggering dose is usually lower.10,12,13 Prior to presentation to allergy services, anaphylaxis occurs in 7%.10

The severity of allergic reactions correlates with the amount of egg protein exposure15; as determined by the amount of egg protein ingested and the degree of processing (baked in wheat, cooked or raw, cooking duration and temperature).
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0049
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Baked egg as an ingredient in sponge cake would mostly cause a mild cutaneous reaction.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0050
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Skin contact to raw egg may induce local cutaneous reactions.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0051
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Systemic reactions have been reported when egg white has been applied to skin for the treatment of nappy rash.16 Ingestion of raw or undercooked egg triggers more severe clinical reactions than well-cooked egg.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0052
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: One death due to egg allergy has been reported in an adult patient in the UK since 1992.17,18 In children with eczema who are allergic to egg protein, dietary exclusion of egg results in improvement of their eczema.19 Clinical case examples of egg allergy presenting with varying degrees of severity are described in Appendix S1.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0053
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Egg allergic patients requiring referral to an allergy clinic are defined in Box 1.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0054
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Note: Early referral is beneficial as a delay in baked egg introduction may limit the development of tolerance.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0055
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
#### 6 | DIAGNOSIS

Acute clinical signs have usually resolved by the time the patient reaches medical attention.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0056
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
The clinical diagnosis is, therefore, made

by a typical history of erythema, urticaria, angio-oedema and/or vomiting with rapid onset (usually within minutes) after ingestion of egg.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0057
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Children with a clear history of a mild reaction to egg can be diagnosed and managed in a primary care setting without further testing.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0058
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Only children with moderate-severe reactions, or where the history remains unclear, require further investigation to confirm and manage egg allergy.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0059
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
7 | INVESTIGATIONS

- 7.1 | Skin prick test

Skin prick testing (SPT) has a poor positive predictive value as a screening tool in the absence of a suspected allergic reaction to egg.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0060
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: SPT using commercially available standardized whole egg reagent should only be carried out if there is clinical suspicion of egg allergy.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0061
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: SPT weal size does not correlate with clinical severity.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0062
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Traditionally, cut-off levels for egg white SPT weal size of ≥3 mm8,20 have been used to support a clinical diagnosis of egg allergy.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0063
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Higher cut-off levels are associated with higher specificity and positive predictive values, e.g., a SPT weal size of 5 mm to egg white is 100% diagnostic in a child under 2 years of age.21 Cut-off values for prick to prick testing with raw egg are reported as ≥13 mm.22 Skin testing with raw egg does not predict tolerance to baked egg in egg-allergic children23.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0064
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: It is not standardized and there is a risk of severe reactions, so is not routinely recommended outside research settings.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0065
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Skin prick testing using a slurry of baked egg had a high negative predictive value for a negative baked egg challenge in one study.24 It is not routinely used in clinical practice.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0066
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
- 7.2 | Egg-specific IgE


When skin prick testing is not available, measurement of eggspecific IgE may be carried out in patients with a history of moderate/severe reactions to egg containing food, to confirm a clinical suspicion of egg allergy.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0067
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: It is not possible to identify a cut-off for serum-specific IgE because of a lack of consistency between studies.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0068
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Although there is a demonstrable relationship between serum IgE levels and challenge outcome within studies, there is poor agreement between centres.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0069
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: With so many interfering variables, these cut- off levels are not applicable to a general population.

chunks.text:
Low levels of egg-specific IgE may be found in children without clinical egg allergy.13 The measurement of egg-specific IgE in the absence of a history of egg ingestion is discouraged as, in this circumstance, the test has poor specificity and low negative predictive value; cautious home introduction or oral challenge will subsequently be required if the egg-specific IgE level is positive but low.8 Measurement of peanut-specific IgE should be included in infants with moderate/severe egg allergy to guide peanut allergy prevention advice.25

#### 7.3 | Egg component testing

The egg white components are ovomucoid (Gal d 1), ovalbumin (Gal d 2), ovotransferrin (Gal d 3), lysozyme (Gal d 4) and livetin (Gal d 5).
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0073
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Ovomucoid (Gal d 1) is heat stable and immunodominant.2,3 The role of component allergens in predicting tolerance to baked egg white, or resolution of egg allergy in routine clinical practice has yet to be established.24 Persisting egg allergy is associated with a positive Gal d 1, and a level ≥11 kU/L indicates a high risk of reacting to cooked and raw egg.3 Gal d 1 is also a good indicator of whether the child is allergic only to raw egg, or to both cooked and raw egg.26 The acquisition of tolerance to egg is associated with a decrease in IgE to egg white and Gal d 1.27 When using test results to identify children at a high risk of anaphylaxis, although egg white sIgE levels are more sensitive, Gal d 1 has better positive predictive value and specificity.28 The current evidence suggests that egg components are rarely needed for the routine diagnosis and management of egg allergy in children but can be a useful adjunct for the assessment of egg allergy resolution in adults (Box 2).
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0074
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
8 | MANAGEMENT

- 8.1 | Avoidance diets

Eggs served in a recognizable form are relatively easy to avoid.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0075
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: They are used as an ingredient of many manufactured foods; therefore, food labels must be consistently checked.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0076
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Uncommon sources of egg include quorn, confectionary and egg hidden in a food, usually ‘egg free’, e.g., pizza dough.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0077
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Extra care needs to be taken with foods sold loose (non-pre-packed) as there may be risk of cross-contamination.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0078
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Individuals with severe egg allergy will need to completely avoid food sold loose/on buffets.

chunks.text: All species of egg (e.g.

chunks.text: quail/duck) are given the generic name ‘egg’ on a label.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0081
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Verbal and written advice on avoidance of egg products should be provided (see Appendices S2 and S3).
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0082
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
- 8.2 | Allergen labelling

Egg is one of the 14 allergens required by EU legislation30 to be declared on the labels of all packaged foods manufactured and sold within the EU, however, small the amount.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0083
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Egg must be emphasized in bold in the ingredient list.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0084
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Other terms for egg include albumin, ovalbumin, globulin, ovoglobulin, livetin, ovomucin, vitellin, ovovitellin, lysozyme and alpha-livetin.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0085
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: These are not allowed to be substituted for the term ‘egg’.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0086
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Knowledge of these terms may be useful for detecting egg protein in non-EU products.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0087
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
- 8.3 | Breastfeeding and egg allergy


Most breastfeeding mothers with egg-allergic children should continue to breastfeed on an unrestricted diet.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0088
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
Egg protein from the maternal diet is detectable in breast milk and may cause reactions in

a very small number of infants.31,32 A trial of maternal egg-free diet may be helpful in the following circumstances:

- 1.

chunks.text: Infants with persistent eczema poorly responsive to treatment, where egg is a known or suspected trigger.

chunks.text:
#### 8.4 | Cross-reactivity between eggs from hens and other bird species

Skin test reactivity to other avian eggs (especially quail and duck) is common in children with hen's egg allergy.33 It is generally accepted that those avoiding hen's egg should also avoid eggs from other avian species, such as duck, goose and quail.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0094
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
There are case reports of reactions to quail, duck and goose egg in those who are not allergic to hen's eggs.34,35

chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0095
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: In practice, adrenaline autoinjectors are rarely required for children with egg allergy.10 The minority of children, who have had severe reactions with evidence of airway narrowing (e.g.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0096
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: wheeze, voice change, choking) or hypotension, should be provided with injectable adrenaline 39–41 and their families reviewed annually by an allergy specialist.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0097
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Children with egg allergy and asthma, requiring regular preventative treatment with inhaled corticosteroids, should also be considered for an adrenaline autoinjector.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0098
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
Families should receive training in how to use their emergency medication, including demonstration with a trainer device and provision of a management plan.41

Adults and young people with persisting egg allergy should be re-assessed, especially prior to a move away from home, for example, to attend university, join the armed forces or travel overseas.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0099
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: They should be provided with updated information about dietary management and the need for an adrenaline autoinjector reviewed.

chunks.text:
9 | RESOLUTION OF EGG ALLERGY

#### 8.5 | When to refer to a dietician

Eggs are a good source of energy, protein, B vitamins and vitamin D, which is important in calcium homeostasis and bone health.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0101
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Those who are not regularly exposed to sunlight benefit from having rich sources of vitamin D in the diet.36 Although it may appear easy to take supplements or substitute other foods, many composite foods may contain eggs; adherence may be difficult without adversely affecting nutritional intake or quality of life.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0102
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
Therefore, whilst the exclusion of eggs does not necessarily lead to nutritional deficiency, a registered dietician should be involved if the diet is also compromised by the exclusion of other foods due to multiple food allergies, lifestyle or religious reasons.37

Patients/families often wish to discuss avoidance in more detail, for example, with regard to specialist replacement products, recipes, eating out or management of children's parties.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0103
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Egg- allergic children have a two-fold increased risk of accidental reactions to egg, where there is no dietetic involvement in counselling the family.38 Dieticians provide valuable advice following hospital-based food challenges.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0104
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: They play an important role in reintroduction plans, especially in advising on home-baked egg ladder progression (Figure 1) and alternative ideas when common baked egg food (such as cake) is disliked (Classification of egg containing foods, Figure 2).
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0105
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Contact with a dietician, 6 months after starting home introduction using the egg ladder, to assess progress is beneficial.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0106
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
#### 8.6 | Provision of emergency medication and treatment plans

All families with egg-allergic children should have an appropriate oral antihistamine available, preferably a second generation, non-drowsy

- 9.1 | Prediction of resolution

At 1 year of age, complete resolution of egg allergy is more likely in children who can tolerate baked egg than those who continue to react.42 The phenotyping of egg allergy (baked egg tolerant vs.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0107
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
allergic) has prognostic implications and eases dietary restrictions.42 Children with mild/moderate egg allergy or with cutaneous reactions only are more likely to resolve.43

Persistence of egg allergy is associated with respiratory or multisystem symptoms, high egg specific IgE, presence of other food allergies or atopic co-morbidities.43–46 Sensitization to multiple egg allergen components, Gal d 1, Gal d 2, Gal d 3 or Gal d 5, may identify children at risk of persistent egg allergy.47

- 9.2 | Natural history of resolution


Egg allergy resolves spontaneously in many affected children over several years, whereas in adults it tends to persist.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0108
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
Allergy to wellcooked egg resolves in about one third of children by 3 years of age, and two-thirds by 6 years (Figure 3).10 The rate of resolution varies between studies42,43,48,49 and egg allergy may continue until the teens.10 Systematic reviews suggest that the median age of resolution is 6–9 years, with 68% of egg-allergic individuals experiencing resolution by the age of 16 years.50

Tolerance to well-processed (baked or lightly cooked) egg occurs long before tolerance to uncooked egg (Figure 3).
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0109
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Children who can tolerate baked egg may continue to react to lightly cooked egg.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0110
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Children outgrow allergy to well-cooked egg approximately twice as quickly as they outgrow allergy to uncooked egg.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0111
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Establishing the former is important to allow relaxation of dietary restrictions and may help establish tolerance.

#### 9.3 | Reintroduction of egg into the diet

Most children with mild egg allergy tolerate gradual staged home introduction according to an egg ladder (Figure 1).
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0125

chunks.text: Baked egg introduction improves quality of life for egg-allergic children, enhances the natural development of tolerance and de-restricts the diet.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0126
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
The speed with which egg allergy resolves varies between individuals, and therefore the timing and appropriateness of egg reintroduction

should be individually assessed.46 Egg-allergic children who can tolerate baked egg at diagnosis and continue to consume baked egg achieve tolerance earlier than those who continue to avoid all forms of egg.51 In children with previous mild reactions and no asthma, the introduction of baked egg into the diet at home from 12 months of age is safe and may support the development of tolerance.52–55 Reintroduction should not be attempted within 6 months of a significant reaction to egg.

chunks.text: Reintroduction at home should not be attempted when there have been severe gastrointestinal, respiratory or cardiovascular symptoms during previous reactions, when only a trace amount has ever been ingested, in the presence of severe eczema (covering >40% of the body), severe multisystem allergic disease or there is ongoing asthma (Box 4).
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0143
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: In these patients, hospital egg challenge should be considered.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0144
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: A more cautious approach should be taken with older children who have been on an exclusion diet for a long time.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0145
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Children who tolerate cooked egg may still react to raw or undercooked egg.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0146
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
There are case reports of children who, following a negative cooked egg challenge, later have severe reactions to raw egg.56 Egg introduction or challenge should not be deferred for concern of increasing sensitization.43

Children undergoing hospital-based baked egg challenges rarely experience anaphylaxis requiring treatment with adrenaline; 2% in one study of 236 children.57 Adrenaline was not required in 181 hospital-based egg challenges.10

A recent study of 678 children undergoing hospital-based egg challenges identified two patients who satisfied BSACI criteria for home reintroduction, and experienced airway symptoms (personal communication – Aljneibi Shaikha).
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0147
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: These hospital challenges employed higher starting doses of egg protein (estimated 200-mg egg protein) and rapid dose escalation compared to gradual low-dose home introduction (estimated starting dose 20-mg egg protein).
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0148
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Patients selected for hospital-based food challenges differ from those selected for home introduction (where those with asthma or a history of severe reactions are excluded).
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0149
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: The dose escalation occurs over a shorter period (a dose every few minutes compared to once- a-day increments) and the starting dose of egg for hospitalbased challenges is considerably higher than that proposed for home introduction.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0150
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: The risk of anaphylaxis in young children being given clear guidance on low-dose baked egg being gradually built up according to a ladder is minimal.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0151
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: In 211 children undergoing home-baked egg introduction, there were no reports of anaphylaxis (H. Ball – personal communication).
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0152
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: We emphasize that home introduction regimes should employ a gradual, staged, low dose approach, according to the egg ladder, rather than rapid escalation as used in hospital-based challenges.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0153
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: As the starting dose for home introduction (estimated 20-mg egg protein) is extremely low, if a reaction were to occur, the symptoms would be mild.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0154
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: We do not advocate testing for egg allergy in children who have no documented reactions to egg; however, children who are allergically sensitized to egg, in the absence of having a documented reaction to egg, should introduce baked egg into their diet at home.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0155
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: If they react, they should be managed as egg allergic.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0156
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
#### 9.5 | Children with severe egg allergy

Children with severe egg allergy, severe multisystem allergic disease, faltering growth (Box 4) or egg allergy persisting beyond the time of usual resolution (6–7 years) should be followed up periodically to assess the likelihood of resolution and to refresh avoidance advice and emergency medication training.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0157
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: A history of any accidental exposure should be sought and SPTs or specific IgE repeated.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0158
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: There are no prospective studies based on specific IgE levels, to advise when to challenge these children.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0159
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
It is reasonable to attempt reintroduction if there has been no significant recent clinical reaction, accompanied by a reduction in SPT wheal size or serum-specific IgE over time.58

These children should have a supervised challenge in hospital and not at home.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0160
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Supervised baked egg challenge should be using a one egg per eight fairy cake recipes in the first instance.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0161
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: There may be exceptions, for example, if a child has had a subsequent mild reaction after significant accidental exposure.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0162
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Children on biologics for asthma should be considered for food challenge once their asthma control has improved.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0163
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
#### 9.6 | Oral immunotherapy

Egg immunotherapy is a deliberate attempt, using regular ingestion of egg, usually with increasing amounts, to generate tolerance to egg in a patient with established egg allergy (usually over 5 years of age).
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0164
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Several studies have demonstrated the safety and efficacy of egg oral immunotherapy (OIT).22,59–62 It is time consuming for clinicians and requires significant commitment for families.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0165
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Desensitization occurs, although tolerance may not be maintained after withdrawal of treatment.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0166
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
A Cochrane review in 2018 commented that studies were small, and the quality of evidence is low.63,64 There are no standardized protocols and a high incidence of adverse events.63,65 In one study, adrenaline was required in 26% of children.65 Early discontinuation is associated with underlying asthma, higher specific IgE and lower threshold during double-blind, placebo-controlled food challenge.65 Ovomucoid IgE >8.85 kU/L indicated a 95% probability of early discontinuation or ongoing reactions over time.65

More recent protocols achieve tolerance in 50% of patients.60,66 The benefits are sustained for up to 5 years after treatment.66 Daily dosing is more effective than weekly dosing.67 Low pre-treatment levels of egg white and ovomucoid IgE predict sustained unresponsiveness following egg immunotherapy.68 Decrease in size of SPT and increase in egg-specific IgG4 over time predicts tolerance in children being treated with egg OIT.61 Ovalbumin IgG4 and Ovalbumin IgE/ IgG4 ratio may be useful to predict the development of tolerance to egg in oral immunotherapy.65

EAACI does not currently recommend egg OIT as a treatment to achieve long-term tolerance in children with persistent egg allergy.69 Egg oral immunotherapy should only be undertaken in highly specialized allergy centres.69

- 10 | EGG ALLERGY IN ADULTS

In contrast to egg allergy in children, egg allergy in adults is likely to be severe and long lasting.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0167
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: It is due to either persistent childhood egg allergy or to true adult-onset egg allergy, which is rare.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0168
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
Adults with persistence of childhood egg allergy have more sequential than conformational IgE epitopes of ovomucoid.70

Adult-onset egg allergy may be:

- 1.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0169
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
New onset adult egg allergy after eggs have been tolerated for years.71
- 2.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0170
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Part of the bird-egg syndrome (a combination of bird-feather sensitization and egg allergy) with an allergy to egg yolk.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0171
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: ‘Bird egg syndrome’ was originally described in subjects, mainly women, who were sensitized to egg yolk and bird (budgerigar and hen) feathers.72 This syndrome is seen in subjects who are exposed to caged birds or pigeons.73 The allergen responsible is alpha livetin (chicken serum albumin, Gal d 5), found in large amounts in egg yolk.74 Typically, patients develop upper and lower respiratory symptoms on exposure to birds and gastrointestinal symptoms with chicken meat or lightly cooked eggs.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0172
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Patients should receive egg avoidance advice, emergency medication and be trained in its use.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0173
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0174
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
Occupational, for example, in workers from the baking industry, who develop sensitization by inhalation.75


There is little information on the prognosis of adult egg allergy and patients should be seen periodically to repeat specific IgE and to update training in the use of emergency medication.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0175
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Older children or adults with a pre-existing egg allergy, presenting to the adult clinic for the first time, should be assessed for the likely resolution of egg allergy.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0176
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Component testing can be useful in determining whether an OFC is feasible, with a negative test to Gal d 1 (ovomucoid), suggesting that a baked egg challenge might be tolerated.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0177
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Although systematic review data suggest that 30% of egg-allergic children will continue to have persisting egg allergy after the age of 16 years, there are no data on continued resolution in young adults.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0178
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
Clinical experience shows that although it persists in some and may be lifelong, many others may have partly or wholly resolving egg allergy, even in their late 20' s. It is extremely important to establish the likelihood of tolerance with oral food challenges, as reactions can be severe and fatal anaphylaxis to egg has been reported in an adult patient.76

- 11 | OTHER EGG-RELATED CONDITIONS


- 11.1 | Egg allergy and asthma


Children with egg allergy are at increased risk of other allergic diseases especially asthma (odds ratio 5.0).77 A careful history should, therefore, be taken to enquire about respiratory symptoms.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0179
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
The presence of asthma may increase the potential severity

of accidental egg reactions and excellent asthma control should be a priority.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0180
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
#### 11.2 | Egg allergy as a risk factor for peanut allergy

Infants with egg allergy are at risk of developing peanut allergy.

chunks.text: The introduction of regular high-dose peanut into the diet of egg-allergic children under 11 months of age reduces the incidence of peanut allergy at 5 years of age.25 Introduction of peanut in children with egg allergy is discussed in the BSACI Early weaning guidance.78 Infants undergoing SPT or measurement of specific IgE to egg proteins should also be tested for peanut sensitization, and peanut containing food introduced alongside other solid foods from around 6 months of age.

chunks.text:
#### 11.3 | Egg allergy and Eosinophilic oesophagitis

Children and adults with eosinophilic oesophagitis (EoE) respond to elimination of common food allergens, including egg.79 Cow's milk and wheat are the most likely triggers of EoE, but a large multicentre study of both children and adults reported that 15% of the subjects had reactions to egg.79 Egg may be a relevant trigger in 35% of children and 26–36% of adults.80–82 Egg avoidance is usually included as part of an empiric four or six food elimination diet.79 Egg SPT is a poor predictor of egg as a trigger for EoE.83

EoE has been reported as a complication of egg immunotherapy.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0183
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: This is usually reversible after early diagnosis and stopping the immunotherapy product.84 There is no evidence that home introduction of egg will cause EoE.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0184
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
#### 11.4 | Use of Propofol in egg-allergic patients

A commonly used formulation of Propofol contains egg lecithin, derived from egg yolk.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0185
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
Propofol administration is safe in adult patients with egg allergy, or who are sensitized to egg.80,85 In a study of propofol administration in egg-allergic children, one child with anaphylaxis to egg developed urticaria and erythema on two occasions after the administration of propofol.86 Propofol is safe to use in children with egg allergy,.87,88

#### 11.5 | FPIES to egg

Food Protein-Induced Enterocolitis syndrome (FPIES) is a rare form of severe delayed type food allergy, thought to be non-IgE mediated, that leads to recurrent vomiting, fluid loss, dehydration, and shock, normally within 4 h of ingestion.89 Egg is a common food trigger for FPIES both in the UK and elsewhere,90 30% of infants with milk or soya FPIES also react to egg protein.91 The diagnosis is made on clinical history.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0186
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: It is safe to use and is recommended to be given to children with egg allergy in any setting, including primary care and schools76 (Department of health, 2017).

chunks.text: There are no safety data on children who have experienced anaphylaxis to egg, requiring intensive care admission and therefore, these children should be referred to a specialist for supervised immunization or, where available, consider an egg-free influenza vaccine in primary care for children over 9 (Lamb Drugs 2019).

chunks.text:
#### 12.2 | Yellow fever vaccine

#### 12 | IMMUNIZATION OF EGG-ALLERGIC CHILDREN AND ADULTS

Hen's egg proteins are found in low amounts in most Influenza vaccines and the Yellow Fever vaccine.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0191
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: The measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine is cultured in chick embryo fibroblast cell culture and not from hen eggs themselves.94 It does not contain hen egg allergens in clinically relevant quantities.95,96 Chapter 6 of the UK Department of Health Green Book, Immunization Against Infectious Disease97 gives advice on immunizing egg-allergic patients.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0192
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Most adults and children with egg allergy can be safely immunized in primary care.

chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

The exceptions that require referral for specialist supervision are those who require:

- 1.

chunks.text:
#### 12.1 | Influenza vaccine

Most Influenza vaccines are derived from the extra-embryonic fluid of chicken embryos inoculated with specific types of influenza virus.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0198
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
The vaccines contain measurable quantities of ovalbumin (egg white protein) which vary between batches and manufacturers.98,99 As vaccine manufacture has improved, reports of egg-related allergic reactions to influenza vaccines are now largely historical.88

Most current influenza vaccines contain very low amounts of ovalbumin (<0.12 mcg/ml or <0.06 mcg in a 0.5 ml dose) and can be administered safely in primary care by the intramuscular route, even in those with a previous history of anaphylaxis to egg.100,101 Egg ovalbumin content of current influenza vaccine can be found in the Summary of Product Characteristic (SPC) for the vaccine, or from the May issue of the current year of Vaccine102 preceding the immunization season.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0199
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
The ovalbumin content of influenza vaccines for the forthcoming influenza season is published annually by Public Health England.103

The intranasal live attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) is also grown in hen's egg, and therefore, contains egg protein.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0200
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

It is safe to administer in children with egg allergy.76 The ovalbumin content

Yellow Fever is a mosquito-borne viral haemorrhagic fever endemic to central Africa and South and Central America.

chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Infection of nonimmune travellers can lead to severe symptoms in up to half of infected persons (Department of Health, 2018).
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0202
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0203
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Yellow Fever vaccine is administered through a network of Yellow Fever Vaccination Centres105 who issue certificates of immunization ahead of travel.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0204
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: The Yellow Fever Vaccine (YFV) is a live vaccine cultured in hen's eggs and contains residual egg proteins.106 Immunization is relatively contraindicated in egg allergy as most allergic reactions to the vaccine are thought to be related to egg allergy, although other allergens such as gelatine are theoretically possible.107 The rate of anaphylaxis is 1 in 238 000 doses of YFV alone and 1 in 131 000 when YFV is co-administered with other vaccines.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0205
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: The potential fatal sequelae from yellow fever means that vaccination should at least be considered.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0206
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Adults and children with egg allergy who require YFV should be assessed in a specialist allergy centre, ideally at least 2 months prior to travel.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0207
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Specialist allergy centres should work in collaboration with their local Yellow Fever Vaccination Centre to source the vaccine and provide certification for their patients.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0208
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: Allergy centres with high throughput may wish to train and register as a Yellow Fever Vaccination Centre, in collaboration with other stakeholders within the hospital, such as infectious diseases and occupational health specialists.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0209
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
Further details on registration as an YFVC can be obtained from the National Travel Health Network and Centre (NATHNAC).108

There are several approaches to YFV immunization of an eggallergic individual, directed by local practice and risk assessment.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0210
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: A proposed travel history should be taken with confirmation of requirement for YFV immunization by the YFVC, who will also be responsible for issuing a certificate of immunization.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0211
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
Initial investigations may include skin prick testing to egg reagent and undiluted YFV, progressing to intradermal testing should initial skin tests be negative.88,109,110 Negative intradermal tests (at 1:10 or 1:100 dilution) predict tolerance of the vaccine.109,110 A two dose schedule can be used depending upon risk assessment.110

Positive skin or intradermal testing to the vaccine suggests allergic reactivity and requires a more cautious approach.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0212
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text: If no further immunization is preferred, a certificate of exemption can be issued by the YFVC.
chunks.chunk_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy_chunk_0213
chunks.doc_id: GUIDELINE - Leech et al. - 2021 - BSACI 2021 guideline for the management of egg allergy

chunks.text:
However, in the face of a positive IDT to YFV, the individual may still seroconvert without further immunization, and the
